purpose: Single crate calibration; wider prop batch remains unapproved
prompt:
Reimagine the CRATE sprite in Image 1 using the exact visual world of Image 2 (the dark StarNet bridge). Image 3 is an approved workstation from that same game. This is a GAME-SCALE sprite material and shape refinement, not a large standalone concept illustration.

Image 1 is the STRUCTURE AND CAMERA LOCK: preserve its full outer envelope, width-to-height ratio, front-to-back alignment and short skids. Preserve the large horizontal lid in the upper roughly 45% of the silhouette and the south/front face in the lower roughly 50%. Parallel horizontal edges, chamfered corners, no visible side face, no perspective convergence, no diagonal/isometric rotation. The native opaque silhouette is 26 units wide and 22 high, anchored along the bottom; at game size it must fit that exact envelope. The upper area is a HORIZONTAL TOP PLANE viewed from above, not a tall vertical back wall.

Keep this immediately recognizable as a sturdy mundane shipping crate: FIVE clearly separated vertical ribs on the front, TWO horizontal reinforcing bands, ONE substantial central locking latch, broad shallow channels on the lid and two short skids. Match the reference bridge's worn cool dark steel, subdued edge highlights and understated surface wear. Use broad readable planes and a few purposeful details. The original low-resolution shapes can become crisp, finely finished forms, but keep their visual hierarchy. Do not cover the object in little rivets, gold trim, pipes, ornament, tiny panels or busy scratches. At normal station zoom the lid, ribs and latch must remain distinct. Restrained material detail similar in scale and contrast to the approved workstation, less ornate because it is a plain crate. No brass colorway, no colored lights, no screen, labels, glowing mark, handles sticking outside the envelope, extra compartments or invented machinery.

ONE complete isolated prop with real transparent RGBA alpha. No floor, cast shadow, room, halo, text, checkerboard background or other objects. Preserve a modest low-contrast dark-material finish; avoid polished photoreal product-shot lighting. Do not enlarge or redesign the crate into a giant cabinet.
